curriculum.title: Module 2 - Food Fraud Vulnerability Assessment (FFVA)

items.label: Module 2 - Food Fraud Vulnerability Assessment (FFVA)
items.description:
This module provides a practical understanding of Food Fraud Vulnerability Assessment (FFVA) under FSSC 22000 Version 6, Section 2.5.4.1. It explains how organizations identify, assess, and prioritize food fraud vulnerabilities across raw materials, ingredients, products, processes, suppliers, and supply chains.

The module focuses on applying a defined methodology, involving a trained multidisciplinary team, evaluating vulnerability factors, identifying significant vulnerabilities, and linking assessment results to an effective food fraud mitigation plan. It helps learners understand FFVA as a formal, documented, site-specific, and auditable process rather than a generic checklist exercise.
items.about: This lesson explains the purpose and practical application of Food Fraud Vulnerability Assessment under FSSC 22000 Version 6. It helps learners understand how vulnerabilities are identified, evaluated, documented, and linked to mitigation planning using a structured and evidence-based approach.

curriculum.title: Module 3 - Determining Significant Vulnerabilities

items.label: Module 3 - Determining Significant Vulnerabilities
items.description:
This module explains how to determine significant food fraud vulnerabilities after completing a Food Fraud Vulnerability Assessment under FSSC 22000 Version 6, Section 2.5.4.1. It helps learners understand which vulnerabilities require formal mitigation and how significance decisions should be made using structured, evidence-based logic.

The module covers practical decision factors such as economic attractiveness, fraud history, detectability, supply-chain complexity, current controls, and supplier-related risks. It also explains how to document decisions clearly, avoid assumption-based judgments, and link significant vulnerabilities directly to the food fraud mitigation plan.
learningOutcomes: Explain the meaning of significant food fraud vulnerability.
Distinguish between general vulnerabilities and vulnerabilities requiring formal mitigation.

Document significance decisions in a clear, consistent, and traceable manner.
Identify common weaknesses in significance evaluation.
Evaluate food fraud cases using evidence-based logic.
Link significant vulnerabilities to suitable mitigation measures.
Strengthen audit readiness through credible and defensible significance decisions.
items.about: This lesson explains how organizations move from identifying food fraud vulnerabilities to deciding which ones are significant and need formal mitigation. It focuses on structured decision-making, documented logic, audit evidence, and the connection between significance evaluation and mitigation planning.

curriculum.title: Module 4 - Food Fraud Mitigation Measures and Mitigation Planning

items.label: Module 4 - Food Fraud Mitigation Measures and Mitigation Planning
items.description:
This module explains how to convert the results of a Food Fraud Vulnerability Assessment (FFVA) into a documented and auditable food fraud mitigation plan under FSSC 22000 Version 6, Section 2.5.4.2. It helps learners understand how mitigation measures should be selected, documented, verified, reviewed, and linked to significant food fraud vulnerabilities.

The module covers the key elements of a strong mitigation plan, including mitigation actions, responsibilities, verification procedures, records, review triggers, and FSMS support. It also explains how organizations can keep the plan updated when suppliers, market conditions, legislation, or fraud intelligence change. Special focus is given to supplier assurance expectations for FII organizations.

items.description:
This module explains how food fraud mitigation should be integrated into the Food Safety Management System (FSMS) rather than treated as a separate activity. It focuses on the support required under FSSC 22000 Version 6, Section 2.5.4.2(b), including training, internal audits, management review, verification, records, corrective action, and continual improvement.

The module helps learners understand the role of a multidisciplinary food fraud team, the importance of competence and awareness, and the need for clear communication, ownership, and escalation pathways. It also explains how weak FSMS integration can reduce the effectiveness of even a well-prepared food fraud mitigation plan.
items.about:
This lesson explains how food fraud mitigation is supported through the wider FSMS. Learners will understand how training, competence, internal audits, management review, records, communication, and corrective actions help ensure that food fraud controls are actually implemented and maintained.

The lesson also highlights why food fraud responsibilities should not depend on one person only. It shows how different functions such as procurement, QA, receiving, operations, technical teams, and management contribute to effective food fraud control.
learningOutcomes: Explain how the food fraud mitigation plan is supported by the FSMS.
Identify FSMS elements that support food fraud mitigation.
Understand the role of training, records, audits, review, and corrective action.
Recognize the importance of a multidisciplinary food fraud team.
Distinguish between HACCP team competence and food fraud team competence.
Evaluate whether food fraud team training is adequate and audit-ready.
Understand the need for wider awareness across procurement, QA, receiving, operations, and management.
Explain the importance of ownership, communication, review, and escalation pathways.
Recognize how food fraud should be included in internal audits and management review.
Identify records needed to demonstrate implementation and effectiveness.
Detect common weaknesses such as one-person ownership, missing training evidence, and poor audit coverage.
Judge whether weak competence or poor FSMS integration can affect the mitigation plan.

curriculum.title: Module 6 — Implementation (Advanced Food Fraud Mitigation and Auditing FSSC 22000:2018 VERSION 6)

items.label: Video — Operational best practices on the job
items.description:
This module prepares learners to audit food fraud mitigation under FSSC 22000 Version 6 using a practical, evidence-based approach. It explains how auditors should review the Food Fraud Vulnerability Assessment (FFVA), evaluate significance decisions, assess mitigation measures, and verify whether the system is properly implemented and supported by the FSMS.

The module focuses on practical audit judgement through document review, interviews, records sampling, supplier evidence, internal audits, management review, performance evaluation, and emergency preparedness. It helps learners move beyond basic paperwork review and develop clear, technically sound audit conclusions.
items.about:
This lesson explains how to audit food fraud mitigation systems under FSSC 22000 Version 6. Learners will understand how to review FFVA, check the logic behind significant vulnerabilities, verify mitigation measures, and assess whether food fraud controls are supported by the wider FSMS.

The lesson also helps learners understand how to collect audit evidence through documents, records, interviews, supplier information, internal audits, and management review outputs.
learningOutcomes: Interpret FSSC 22000 food fraud requirements in audit contexts.
Verify whether the FFVA is documented, scoped, and methodology-based.
Evaluate the logic used to identify significant vulnerabilities.
Assess whether mitigation measures are risk-based and proportionate.
Review mitigation plans for controls, verification procedures, and implementation logic.
Collect objective audit evidence through documents, records, interviews, and supplier information.
Assess team competence, training records, and ownership responsibilities.
Verify FSMS support through internal audits, management review, corrective action, and performance evaluation.
Identify common weaknesses and possible nonconformities.
Write clear, evidence-based audit conclusions linked to FSSC requirements.
Apply structured audit review points with confidence and consistency.
